domain: Building, signing, and installing a personal iOS app with NO Mac — Windows 11 only (verified July 2026). Covers GitHub Actions macOS runners, Mac-free .xcodeproj generation, unsigned xcodebuild + .ipa packaging, Windows-side re-signing (Sideloadly / AltStore Classic / SideStore / TrollStore), and the free-Apple-ID entitlement matrix.

capabilities.resolution: macOS 26.4 (25E246); GA since 2026-02-26; macos-latest points at macos-26 as of June 2026
capabilities.notes: Xcode installed: 26.6 (17F113), 26.5 (17F42 = DEFAULT /Applications/Xcode.app), 26.4.1 (17E202), 26.3 (17C529), 26.2 (17C52), 26.1.1 (17B100), 26.0.1 (17A400). SDKs: iphoneos26.5, iphonesimulator26.5, watchos26.5, watchsimulator26.5, macosx26.5. Preinstalled tooling: CocoaPods 1.17.0, Fastlane 2.237.0, xcbeautify 3.2.1, SwiftFormat 0.62.1. XcodeGen/Tuist are NOT preinstalled (inferred from the readme tool list — add a `brew install xcodegen` step, ~20-40s).

capabilities.notes: Xcode: 26.3, 26.2, 26.1.1, 26.0.1, 16.4 (16F6 = DEFAULT), 16.3, 16.2, 16.1, 16.0. SDKs: iphoneos18.0-18.5 (Xcode 16.x) and iphoneos26.0-26.2 (Xcode 26.x). capabilities.stream: macOS CI build host — deprecated image
capabilities.resolution: marked Deprecated in the runner-images README
capabilities.notes: Most copy-paste 'unsigned iOS build' workflows on the internet still say macos-14. Do not use it — GitHub keeps at most 2 GA + 1 beta image per OS and macos-14 is past GA. Use macos-15 or macos-26.

capabilities.stream: iOS 27 SDK on CI (bleeding edge / future-proofing)
capabilities.resolution: Image OS macOS 26.5.2 (25F84); Xcode 27.0 beta build 27A5218g at /Applications/Xcode_27_beta_3.app; SDKs iphoneos27.0, iphonesimulator27.0
capabilities.notes: ANSWER TO 'has iOS 27 shipped?': NO. As of July 2026 iOS 26.x is the shipping release (26.5 SDK is what macos-26 ships by default) and iOS 27 is in DEVELOPER BETA (Xcode 27 beta 3). Build against iphoneos26.x and set a 26.0 deployment target; do not target 27 for a device you actually use. Preview images can vanish without notice.

capabilities.stream: FREE macOS CI minutes — PUBLIC repository
capabilities.api: standard runner labels only (macos-15, macos-26); NOT macos-*-large / -xlarge
capabilities.notes: Verbatim: 'The use of standard GitHub-hosted runners is free: In public repositories' and 'Larger runners are always charged for, even when used by public repositories.' So macos-26 in a public repo = $0.00 forever. The catch is not billing, it's privacy: your source is public. For a quantified-self app keep only CODE in the repo — never health data, never the Apple ID, never a pairing file.

capabilities.stream: FREE macOS CI minutes — PRIVATE repository (real cost math)
capabilities.api: 10x macOS minute multiplier against included minutes; $0.062/min overage (macOS 3-core or 4-core)
capabilities.resolution: Free plan 2,000 included min/mo; Pro/Team 3,000; Enterprise Cloud 50,000
capabilities.notes: THE MATH: included minutes are Linux-equivalent and drain at the OS multiplier (Linux 1x, Windows 2x, macOS 10x). Free plan = 2,000 / 10 = 200 macOS wall-clock minutes/month = TWENTY 10-minute builds, then you pay. Overage: 10 min x $0.062 = $0.62 per build. 4 builds/week beyond the allowance ≈ $10/mo — i.e. private-repo CI costs more per year than the $99 Apple Developer Program that would solve your signing problems. Rates reflect the 1 Jan 2026 repricing. The multiplier is documented in third-party pricing trackers and in GitHub's own multiplier table; the top-level billing page only shows the $/min figures, so cite both.

capabilities.stream: Generate an .xcodeproj without a Mac — RECOMMENDED path
capabilities.api: project.yml -> `brew install xcodegen && xcodegen generate` on the macOS runner
capabilities.resolution: declarative YAML; app target + app-extension targets + entitlements + App Groups all expressible
capabilities.notes:
WINNER for this constraint, because project.yml is PLAIN TEXT you can author blind on Windows and never needs to run locally. Working shape:

name: Probe
options:
  bundleIdPrefix: com.yourname
  deploymentTarget: { iOS: "18.0" }
  createIntermediateGroups: true
settings:
  base:
    DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: ""
    SWIFT_VERSION: "6.0"
    TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY: "1,2"
targets:
  Probe:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    sources: [Probe]
    info:
      path: Probe/Info.plist
      properties:
        NSHealthShareUsageDescription: "Reads your own health data."
        NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription: "Writes your own health data."
        NSMotionUsageDescription: "Reads motion activity."
        UIBackgroundModes: [processing, location, fetch]
        BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers: [com.yourname.Probe.refresh]
    entitlements:
      path: Probe/Probe.entitlements
      properties:
        com.apple.security.application-groups: [group.com.yourname.Probe]
        com.apple.developer.healthkit: true
        com.apple.developer.healthkit.background-delivery: true
    dependencies:
      - target: ProbeWidget
        embed: true
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.yourname.Probe
        REGISTER_APP_GROUPS: YES
  ProbeWidget:
    type: app-extension
    platform: iOS
    sources: [ProbeWidget]
    info:
      path: ProbeWidget/Info.plist
      properties:
        NSExtension:
          NSExtensionPointIdentifier: com.apple.widgetkit-extension
    entitlements:
      path: ProbeWidget/ProbeWidget.entitlements
      properties:
        com.apple.security.application-groups: [group.com.yourname.Probe]
    settings:
      base:
        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.yourname.Probe.Widget
        ALWAYS_EMBED_SWIFT_STANDARD_LIBRARIES: NO
schemes:
  Probe:
    build: { targets: { Probe: all } }

XcodeGen writes the .entitlements plist for you and wires CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS. Extension types available: app-extension, app-extension.intents-service, app-extension.messages, watchkit-extension, watchkit2-extension. `REGISTER_APP_GROUPS: YES` is Apple DTS's fix for App Group provisioning on Xcode 16.4+.

capabilities.stream: Generate an .xcodeproj without a Mac — alternative
capabilities.resolution: full app + extension + entitlement support, richer than XcodeGen
capabilities.notes: Technically more capable but WRONG for this constraint: the manifest is Swift, so you get zero editor/compiler feedback on Windows and every typo costs a full CI round-trip (~10 min). Also heavier install on the runner and it wants a cache/warm step. Use Tuist only if you outgrow XcodeGen.

capabilities.stream: Generate an .xcodeproj without a Mac — do not use
capabilities.notes: SPM has no iOS application product type. It cannot emit an .app bundle, an Info.plist for an app, an entitlements file, or embed an app extension. Use SPM only for your own library targets that the XcodeGen app target then depends on.

capabilities.stream: Generate an .xcodeproj without a Mac — do not use
capabilities.notes: Every file, build phase, and target cross-references others by hand-generated UUID. Adding one extension touches 8+ object graphs (PBXNativeTarget, PBXCopyFilesBuildPhase for the Embed App Extensions phase, PBXTargetDependency, PBXContainerItemProxy, XCConfigurationList x2...). One bad UUID = 'The project is damaged' with no line number. This is the single highest-regret option on Windows.

capabilities.stream: Build the app in CI with NO signing identity
capabilities.resolution: ~4-12 min for a small SwiftUI app incl. brew install xcodegen
capabilities.notes:
Two working shapes.
(A) build (flat products dir):
xcodebuild -project Probe.xcodeproj -scheme Probe -configuration Release -sdk iphoneos -derivedDataPath build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="" build
-> product at build/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Probe.app
(B) archive (cleaner for extensions):
xcodebuild archive -project Probe.xcodeproj -scheme Probe -configuration Release -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -archivePath unsigned.xcarchive CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=""
-> product at unsigned.xcarchive/Products/Applications/Probe.app
All three flags are needed together: REQUIRED=NO alone still lets Xcode try to resolve an identity; the empty CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY is what stops provisioning-profile lookup. Do NOT pass -allowProvisioningUpdates (there is no Apple ID on the runner).

capabilities.stream: Package the unsigned build as an installable .ipa
capabilities.api: mkdir Payload && cp -R Probe.app Payload/ && zip -r Probe.ipa Payload
capabilities.notes: An .ipa is literally a zip with a top-level Payload/ directory. `xcodebuild -exportArchive` CANNOT be used here — it insists on a signing identity and an ExportOptions.plist method, so hand-zipping is the only Mac-free path. Upload with actions/upload-artifact@v4. Sideloadly/AltStore then re-sign the whole bundle on Windows.

capabilities.stream: App extension embedded in the unsigned .ipa
capabilities.api: PlugIns/*.appex inside Probe.app; dependencies: [{target: X, embed: true}]
capabilities.notes: Gotchas that only show up with extensions: (1) set ALWAYS_EMBED_SWIFT_STANDARD_LIBRARIES=NO on every extension target — only the app should carry Frameworks/libswift*.dylib, duplicates produce invalid nested code. (2) With CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO no _CodeSignature/ directories are emitted anywhere, which is actually IDEAL — the Windows re-signer sees a clean tree and does not have to strip stale signatures out of nested bundles. (3) Skip SwiftSupport/ — that is an App Store submission artifact, irrelevant for sideloading.

capabilities.stream: Free Apple ID can sign: app identity
capabilities.framework: Apple developerservices2 / AltSign / Sideloadly / Xcode Personal Team
capabilities.notes: Always present. Prefixed with your Team ID — this is why switching Apple IDs breaks data continuity.

capabilities.stream: Free Apple ID can sign: App Groups (shared container app <-> extension)
capabilities.notes: YES — this is the single most important 'it works' finding. AltSign (the library behind BOTH AltStore and SideStore) registers app groups against a free Apple ID via Apple's internal feature ID APG3427HIY, and AltStore's own error codes 3014 ('The provided app group is invalid') / 3015 ('App group does not exist') / 1012 ('AltStore's shared app group could not be accessed') exist precisely because AltStore itself runs on a free ID with an app group. CONTESTED: several blog posts and search summaries claim personal teams cannot use App Groups, and Xcode's Signing & Capabilities UI is reported to block it. Both can be true — Xcode's UI denylist and the developerservices2 API allowlist are different things, and in a Windows-only workflow you never touch Xcode's UI. Treat App Groups as available. Use iOS-style group IDs (group.com.you.app), NOT $(TeamIdentifierPrefix)group... — Apple DTS explicitly recommends this and it is a known Xcode <16.4 failure mode.

capabilities.stream: Free Apple ID can sign: Keychain Sharing
capabilities.notes: Supported. Note that keychain items themselves are scoped to the access group AND the team prefix — re-signing with the same free Apple ID preserves them.

capabilities.stream: Free Apple ID can sign: debugger attach / JIT
capabilities.notes: Always set on development profiles. This is what makes Sideloadly's 'Enable JIT' feature possible, and it is also why a sideloaded dev-signed app can be debugged.

capabilities.stream: Free Apple ID can sign: Game Center
capabilities.notes: Registerable feature on a free ID per AltSign. Irrelevant for telemetry but it bounds the allowlist.

capabilities.stream: Free Apple ID can sign: Inter-App Audio
capabilities.notes: Deprecated by Apple, but present in AltSign's allowlist — completes the enumeration of the FOUR entitlements + THREE features AltSign supports. That short list IS the practical free-ID entitlement matrix for the AltStore/SideStore path.

capabilities.stream: Free Apple ID can sign: team identifier binding
capabilities.notes: Auto-populated. Load-bearing for the data-survival question: same Apple ID = same team ID = install-over preserves the app container.

capabilities.stream: HealthKit on a free Apple ID — THE decisive unknown
capabilities.api: HKHealthStore; capability 'HealthKit' in Apple's supported-capabilities-ios list
capabilities.permission: NSHealthShareUsageDescription + NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription (Info.plist) and a runtime authorization sheet
capabilities.notes:
GENUINELY CONTESTED — and it decides whether this whole Windows-only free path builds YOUR app or just AN app.
AGAINST (evidence it fails): AltSign enumerates exactly 6 entitlements and 3 features; com.apple.developer.healthkit is NOT among them, so AltStore and SideStore literally cannot request it in a profile. Apple's Choosing a Membership page puts 'Advanced app capabilities and services' behind the $99 program, and supported-capabilities-ios opens with 'The capabilities available to an iOS provisioning profile depend on your program membership.' Apple DTS says the Personal Team has 'significant limitations' and is meant for running from Xcode, not producing .ipa files.
FOR (evidence it works): Apple never publishes HealthKit in any membership-gated list; the documented Personal-Team refusals are capability-specific and the confirmed verbatim error is for Push Notifications ('Personal development teams, including "X", do not support the Push Notifications capability'), not HealthKit. Community reports of the HealthKit sub-options (Background Delivery, Clinical Health Records) being greyed out in Xcode are about those SUB-entitlements, not base HealthKit.
DECISIVE TEST (run it before writing a line of app code): build a 20-line stub with only com.apple.developer.healthkit in the entitlements, sideload with Sideloadly. Three possible outcomes and what each means — (a) install fails with error 0xe8008016 / 'Entitlements are not valid' => the signer preserved the entitlement but the free profile refused it: HealthKit is DEAD on free. (b) installs but HKHealthStore.requestAuthorization immediately fails / the app crashes on first HealthKit call => the signer STRIPPED the entitlement: also dead. (c) the authorization sheet appears => it works, proceed. This single test is worth more than any further reading.

capabilities.stream: Push Notifications on a free Apple ID
capabilities.api: Xcode error: 'Personal development teams, including "NAME", do not support the Push Notifications capability.'
capabilities.notes: DEFINITIVELY UNAVAILABLE — verbatim Xcode error confirmed on Apple's own forums. Consequence for telemetry: no remote push, and no silent background push wake-up. LOCAL notifications (UNNotificationRequest) need no entitlement and DO work — use those.

capabilities.stream: Background execution modes on a free Apple ID
capabilities.api: UIBackgroundModes in Info.plist; BGAppRefreshTask / BGProcessingTask; BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers
capabilities.entitlement: none for audio/location/fetch/processing/bluetooth-central; com.apple.developer.healthkit.background-delivery for HealthKit background delivery
capabilities.notes: Most UIBackgroundModes are pure Info.plist keys with NO entitlement — they work on a free ID. 'Background modes' does appear in Apple's capability list, but the entitlement-bearing members of that family are the push-adjacent ones. Practical rule for a telemetry app: location (always), processing, fetch, bluetooth-central = fine; remote-notification = dead (needs aps-environment).

capabilities.stream: Capabilities that are unavailable or approval-gated regardless
capabilities.notes: Apple's full iOS capability list (all 57): 5G Network Slicing; Access WiFi information; App Attest; App groups; Apple Pay; Associated domains; AutoFill credential provider; Background modes; ClassKit; Communication Notifications; Data protection; DriverKit Family MIDI*; Extended Virtual Addressing; Family Controls (development)*; FileProvider Testing Mode*; Fonts; Game Center; Group Activities; Head Pose; HealthKit; HealthKit Estimate Recalibration; HLS Interstitial Previews; HomeKit; Hotspot; iCloud: CloudKit; iCloud: iCloud documents; iCloud: iCloud key-value storage; ID Verifier - Display Only; In-App Purchase; Increased Debugging Memory Limit; Inter-App Audio; Journaling Suggestions; Keychain sharing; Low Latency HLS; Maps; Matter Allow Setup Payload; MDM Managed Associated Domains; Media Device Discovery; Messages Collaboration; Multipath; NFC Tag Reading; Network extensions; On Demand Install Capable; Personal VPN; Push to Talk; Push notifications; Sensitive Content Analysis; Shared with You; Sign in with Apple; SIM Inserted for Wireless Carriers; Siri; Spatial Audio Profile; Sustained Execution; Time Sensitive Notifications; Wallet; WeatherKit; Wireless Accessory Configuration. (* = development only.) Family Controls requires a separate Apple approval request even on a PAID account — it is not a free-tier question at all. None of these appear in AltSign's allowlist, so none are reachable through the AltStore/SideStore path.

capabilities.stream: Install the .ipa on iPhone from Windows — PRIMARY tool
capabilities.permission: Apple ID + password (+2FA code) entered in the tool; device Trust prompt; Settings > General > VPN & Device Management to trust the cert
capabilities.entitlement: none (it re-signs with a free-team development profile)
capabilities.resolution: USB or Wi-Fi install; auto-refresh via the Sideloadly Daemon
capabilities.notes: STILL WORKS IN 2026. Windows 7/8/10/11 (Win10+ recommended). HARD REQUIREMENT: the WEB versions of iTunes AND iCloud from apple.com — NOT the Microsoft Store versions, which sandbox the folders anisette data is read from and produce 'invalid anisette data' / connection errors. Remote anisette is used by default and transmits only your IP, OS type, and Sideloadly version. Since v0.50.0 the macOS Mail plug-in dependency is gone. App-specific passwords only work with PAID developer IDs when anisette is disabled — with a free ID you must use the real password + 2FA. Features relevant here: 'Remove individual or all app extensions (PlugIns) before install' (i.e. it HANDLES extensions and lets you drop them to save App IDs), bundle-ID/name/icon rewriting, minimum-iOS-version rewriting, dylib/deb/framework/bundle injection, Wi-Fi sideloading, file sharing.

capabilities.stream: Automatic weekly re-sign from Windows — the only documented mechanism
capabilities.resolution: daemon re-signs apps nearing expiry whenever the device is detected (USB, or Wi-Fi if Wi-Fi sideloading is configured)
capabilities.notes: NEGATIVE FINDING, exhaustion stated: Sideloadly exposes NO documented command line. Checked sideloadly.io/faq.html (narrow re-query) and the official github.com/SideloadlyiOS/Sideloadly-Download README — both silent on CLI, scripting, or automation. So 'scheduled task + sideloadly.exe --args' is not a supported plan. The supported plan is: leave the Sideloadly daemon running on the Windows box, keep credentials saved, and have the phone on the same Wi-Fi (or docked) at least once every 7 days. Belt-and-braces: also install AltStore Classic and enable its Background Refresh, so two independent mechanisms are racing to beat the expiry.

capabilities.stream: Install from Windows — alternative with on-device background refresh
capabilities.permission: Apple ID + password; iOS Settings > General > VPN & Device Management trust; iOS 16+ Developer Mode
capabilities.resolution: Wi-Fi refresh; AltStore wakes periodically in the background and refreshes against AltServer
capabilities.notes: Requirements verbatim: 'Download and install the latest version of iTunes and iCloud directly from Apple (not the Microsoft Store).' Enable Wi-Fi sync in iTunes. Credentials go only to Apple. Best-in-class for the 7-day problem because the refresh is initiated BY THE PHONE — the Windows box just has to be awake on the same network. NOTE: AltStore Classic 2.3b1 (Patreon beta) adds on-device sideloading with NO computer at all — you supply an anisette server URL and the phone talks to Apple directly. If that ships stable, the Windows machine drops out of the weekly loop entirely.

capabilities.stream: Install from Windows — alternative, computer-free refresh
capabilities.api: iloader (Windows/macOS/Linux/ChromeOS); LocalDevVPN from the App Store
capabilities.permission: Apple ID; device passcode REQUIRED; VPN profile active during install/refresh
capabilities.resolution: on-device refresh over Wi-Fi; no computer needed after setup
capabilities.notes: IMPORTANT 2026 UPDATE — the old guides are stale. SideStore now uses `iloader` on the computer and `LocalDevVPN` from the App Store; the jitterbugpair.exe + .mobiledevicepairing + StosVPN/WireGuard flow that dominates search results is the LEGACY path. Windows 8+ supported; 32-bit Windows and Windows 10 on ARM are NOT. Wi-Fi required (cellular will not do). 'If using a free Apple Account, SideStore can only install 3 apps (including itself) at a time' — SideStore itself burns one of your three. Data preservation: sideloading the same IPA over an existing install keeps your data. Entitlement handling is AltSign's, i.e. the same 6+3 allowlist.

capabilities.stream: Install from Windows — permanent signing (NOT viable)
capabilities.notes: DEAD for any current device. Verbatim: '16.7.x (excluding 16.7 RC) and 17.0.1+ will NEVER be supported (unless a third CoreTrust bug is discovered, which is unlikely).' An iPhone on iOS 26.x cannot use TrollStore. If it COULD, it would solve everything at once — permanent signing, no 7-day expiry, no 3-app limit, arbitrary entitlements. Do not plan around it.

capabilities.stream: 3 sideloaded apps at a time (free Apple ID)
capabilities.api: AltStore error 2009: 'Cannot activate more than 3 apps with a non-developer Apple ID'
capabilities.resolution: 3 top-level apps; app EXTENSIONS do not count toward this 3
capabilities.notes: 'Due to restrictions by Apple, you can only have 3 sideloaded apps installed on a device at a time.' The sideloader itself (AltStore/SideStore) consumes one slot — Sideloadly does not, since it is a Windows app. So: Sideloadly-only = 3 slots for your apps; SideStore = 2. AltStore's 'deactivate' feature backs up an app's data, removes it, and restores it on reactivation, which lets you rotate more than 3 apps without data loss.

capabilities.stream: 10 App IDs per rolling 7 days (free Apple ID)
capabilities.api: AltStore error 1009 / Apple error 3013: 'You cannot register more than 10 App IDs within a 7 day period'
capabilities.resolution: each App ID expires 7 days after registration, freeing a slot
capabilities.notes: Apple's own Choosing a Membership page confirms: 'App IDs: Limited to 10 at one time, each expires after 7 days' and 'Test devices: Limited to 3 per platform.' CRITICAL ARITHMETIC: app extensions each consume their own App ID — AltStore states sideloading requirements depend on 'the number of app extensions each app contains.' An app + widget + Live Activity + Watch app can burn 4-5 of your 10 in a single install. Design for ONE extension, or zero.

capabilities.stream: 7-day provisioning profile expiry
capabilities.api: free-team development provisioning profile validity = 7 days
capabilities.resolution: 7 days from issuance (365 with a $99 account)
capabilities.notes: WHAT ACTUALLY BREAKS: (1) The app refuses to LAUNCH — 'Unable to Verify App' / the icon greys out. (2) Background execution stops SILENTLY. BGTaskScheduler tasks, significant-location wake-ups, and HealthKit background delivery all work by the SYSTEM RELAUNCHING your app — and that relaunch fails against an expired profile with no user-visible error. So a telemetry app does not gracefully degrade; it just stops collecting, and you find out days later from a gap in the data. Mitigation: write a heartbeat row on every background wake and alarm on staleness. (3) Data DOES survive: the app container is untouched by expiry, and re-signing/reinstalling the same bundle ID with the SAME Apple ID (same Team ID => same application-identifier prefix) installs over the top and keeps everything. Changing Apple IDs changes the team prefix, iOS treats it as a different app, and you must delete first — losing the data.

capabilities.stream: Developer Mode gate on the device
capabilities.notes: On iOS 16+ a free-signed app will not launch until Developer Mode is on; the toggle only appears after a development-signed app has been installed once. SideStore additionally requires the device to HAVE a passcode. Enabling Developer Mode requires a reboot and reduces some device security posture — a real consideration on a phone that holds your health data.

capabilities.stream: Trusting the developer certificate on device
capabilities.api: Settings > General > VPN & Device Management > Developer App > Trust
capabilities.permission: manual user action, cannot be automated
capabilities.resolution: per signing certificate, not per app or per refresh
capabilities.notes: You trust the CERTIFICATE, so a normal weekly profile refresh does not re-prompt. But a free Apple ID has a very small certificate budget — signing from a second machine or a second tool can cause Apple to issue/revoke certs, which instantly kills every app signed by the old one and forces a re-trust. Practical rule: pick ONE Windows machine and ONE tool as the signer of record.

blockers: TrollStore is not an option. Verbatim from the repo: supported versions are '14.0 beta 2 - 16.6.1, 16.7 RC (20H18), 17.0' and '16.7.x (excluding 16.7 RC) and 17.0.1+ will NEVER be supported (unless a third CoreTrust bug is discovered, which is unlikely).' An iPhone on iOS 26.x cannot use it, so permanent signing / unlimited entitlements are off the table entirely. https://github.com/opa334/TrollStore

HealthKit may be unsignable on a free Apple ID — and for a quantified-self app, HealthKit IS the app. AltSign, the signing library behind BOTH AltStore and SideStore, supports exactly six entitlements (application-identifier, keychain-access-groups, com.apple.security.application-groups, get-task-allow, com.apple.developer.team-identifier, inter-app-audio) and three features (gameCenter, App Groups APG3427HIY, Inter-App Audio IAD53UNK2F). com.apple.developer.healthkit appears nowhere. Apple's Choosing a Membership page puts 'Advanced app capabilities and services' behind the $99 program. Counter-evidence exists (Apple never names HealthKit as membership-gated; the only VERBATIM Personal-Team refusal on record is for Push Notifications), so this is contested rather than settled — but it is the one unknown that can invalidate the entire free path. Test it with a 20-line stub BEFORE building anything. https://github.com/rileytestut/AltSign/blob/master/AltSign/Capabilities/ALTCapabilities.m

Push Notifications are definitively impossible on a free Apple ID. Verbatim Xcode error from Apple's forums: 'Personal development teams, including "NAME", do not support the Push Notifications capability.' The aps-environment entitlement cannot be provisioned, which also kills silent remote-push background wake-ups. Local notifications still work (no entitlement). https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/718388

xcodebuild -exportArchive cannot be used to produce the .ipa. It requires a signing identity and an ExportOptions.plist distribution method, neither of which exists on a runner with no Apple ID. The ONLY Mac-free path is to build/archive with signing fully disabled and hand-zip Payload/YourApp.app into a .ipa.

The .ipa CI produces is unsigned and cannot be installed by itself. It is inert until a Windows-side tool (Sideloadly / AltServer / SideStore) re-signs it against your free Apple ID. Any guide that stops at 'here is your unsigned IPA' has not solved the problem.

XcodeGen and Tuist are macOS-only Swift binaries — neither runs on Windows. You author project.yml as plain text locally and run `brew install xcodegen && xcodegen generate` on the macOS runner. This means every project-structure typo costs a full ~10-minute CI round-trip, which is the real argument for XcodeGen's YAML over Tuist's Swift manifest.

Swift Package Manager cannot build an iOS app. There is no application product type — no .app bundle, no app Info.plist, no entitlements wiring, no Embed App Extensions phase. SPM is only usable for your own library targets consumed by an XcodeGen app target.

Sideloadly has no documented command line. Verified against both sideloadly.io/faq.html (re-queried narrowly) and the official SideloadlyiOS/Sideloadly-Download README — both are silent on CLI, scripting, and automation. A Windows Task Scheduler job driving sideloadly.exe is therefore not a supported design. Automation must go through the Sideloadly Daemon's auto-refresh or AltStore's on-device Background Refresh.

Microsoft Store versions of iTunes and iCloud break sideloading. Both Sideloadly and AltStore require the WEB (apple.com) installers; the Store builds sandbox the folders anisette authentication data is read from, producing 'invalid anisette data' and connection failures.
SideStore does not support 32-bit Windows or Windows 10/11 on ARM, and requires the iPhone to have a passcode set. Windows 8+ x64 only.

GitHub's larger runners are billed even on public repositories. Verbatim: 'Larger runners are always charged for, even when used by public repositories.' Free macOS CI only holds for the standard labels (macos-15, macos-26) — never macos-*-large or -xlarge.
runs-on: macos-14 is deprecated and will disappear. Nearly every 'build unsigned iOS IPA on GitHub Actions' example still in circulation pins macos-14. Use macos-15 or macos-26.

Family Controls (com.apple.developer.family-controls) requires an explicit approval request from Apple even on a PAID account, and is marked 'development only' in Apple's capability list. It is not a free-tier question — it is unavailable to you regardless.

iOS 27 has NOT shipped. As of July 2026 iOS 26.x is the shipping release (macos-26 runners default to Xcode 26.5 / iphoneos26.5) and iOS 27 is in developer beta only (Xcode 27 beta 3, build 27A5218g, iphoneos27.0, available on the Preview 'xcode-27' runner image). Do not target the 27 SDK for a phone you actually depend on.
nonObvious: The extension arithmetic is the real budget constraint, not the 3-app limit. Each app EXTENSION consumes its own App ID against the 10-per-7-days ceiling (AltStore: sideloading requirements depend on 'the number of app extensions each app contains'), but extensions do NOT count against the 3-installed-apps limit. So a main app + widget + Live Activity + Watch app can burn 4-5 App IDs in one install, and two bad install attempts in a week can lock you out until IDs age off. Design for at most one extension.

`find build -name '*.app' | head -n 1` — the line in almost every copy-paste unsigned-IPA workflow — is a landmine once you add extensions. In a multi-target build it can grab a Watch app, a test host, or a dependency's product instead of your app. Use the deterministic path: build/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/YourApp.app (for `build`) or unsigned.xcarchive/Products/Applications/YourApp.app (for `archive`). Pick one recipe and hard-code the path.

Building with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO is not just a workaround — it produces a CLEANER artifact for re-signing than a signed build would. No _CodeSignature directories are emitted anywhere in the bundle, including nested .appex and .framework bundles, so the Windows re-signer never has to strip stale nested signatures (a classic source of 'invalid code signature' install failures).

Set ALWAYS_EMBED_SWIFT_STANDARD_LIBRARIES=NO on every app-extension target. Only the containing app should ship Frameworks/libswift*.dylib. Duplicate Swift runtime copies inside PlugIns/*.appex produce invalid nested code that re-signers choke on. Also: skip SwiftSupport/ entirely — it is an App Store submission artifact and irrelevant for sideloading.

Free Apple IDs CAN provision App Groups, contradicting most blog posts. The proof is in AltSign's source: ALTFeatureAppGroups = "APG3427HIY" is Apple's internal developerservices2 feature ID, and AltStore's error codes 3014/3015/1012 exist because AltStore itself runs on a free ID with an app group. What is actually restricted is Xcode's Signing & Capabilities UI — a different denylist. In a Windows-only workflow you never open Xcode, so the UI restriction is irrelevant to you.

Use iOS-style app group IDs (group.com.you.app), never $(TeamIdentifierPrefix)group.com.you.app. Apple DTS explicitly recommends the iOS style and flags the mixed form as a cause of 'Provisioning profile doesn't support the App Groups capability.' Also enable the REGISTER_APP_GROUPS build setting (Xcode 16.4+), which is Apple's own documented fix for app-group provisioning failures.

The 7-day expiry does not degrade gracefully for a telemetry app — it fails SILENTLY. Background collection works by the system relaunching your app (BGTaskScheduler, significant-location changes, HealthKit background delivery). Against an expired profile those relaunches fail with no user-visible error and no notification. You discover the outage days later as a hole in the data. Write a heartbeat timestamp on every background wake and alarm on staleness; do not trust 'the app looks fine on my home screen.'

App data survives re-signing — but ONLY with the same Apple ID. The data container is keyed to the bundle ID plus the Team-ID-prefixed application-identifier. Same free Apple ID => same Team ID => install-over preserves everything. Switch Apple IDs (e.g. to dodge the 10-App-ID limit) and iOS sees a different application-identifier, refuses to install over, and you must delete the app — losing your entire collected history. Never rotate Apple IDs on a data-collecting app.

A free Apple ID has a tiny certificate budget, and signing from a second machine or a second tool can revoke the existing certificate — instantly bricking every app signed by it and forcing a re-Trust on the device. Choose ONE Windows machine and ONE tool as the signer of record, and do not casually try Sideloadly and AltServer and SideStore in the same week.

Two independent refresh mechanisms beat one. Sideloadly's daemon refreshes when it SEES the device (USB or configured Wi-Fi) — it fails if the PC is asleep or the phone is away. AltStore Classic's Background Refresh is initiated BY THE PHONE against AltServer. Running both gives you two chances per week to beat the expiry. Better still: AltStore Classic 2.3b1 adds fully on-device sideloading via a user-supplied anisette server URL, removing the Windows machine from the weekly loop entirely — worth tracking.

Public repo is the correct CI choice for cost ($0 unlimited standard macOS minutes vs 20 free builds/month private), but only if you are disciplined: code in the repo, never health data, never the Apple ID, never a device pairing file. If you cannot commit to that, note that private-repo overage at $0.62/build times ~16 builds/month exceeds the $99/year Apple Developer Program — which would ALSO eliminate the 7-day expiry, the 3-app limit, the 10-App-ID limit, and the entire entitlement question. The free path is the constraint you chose; the honest cost comparison says the paid account is cheaper than heavy private CI.

macos-15's DEFAULT Xcode is still 16.4 (iOS 18.5 SDK) even though Xcode 26.x is installed on the image. If you pin macos-15 and do not run `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_26.3.app`, you will silently build against the iOS 18 SDK and lose every iOS 26 API. macos-26 defaults to Xcode 26.5 and does not have this trap.

The failure mode tells you which layer broke. Install fails with 0xe8008016 / 'Entitlements are not valid' => the signer PRESERVED an entitlement the free profile refuses. Installs fine but the API call fails or crashes at first use => the signer STRIPPED the entitlement to match the profile. Sideloadly (zsign-lineage) tends toward the latter, AltStore/SideStore toward simply not requesting it. Knowing which you got saves a day of guessing.

SideStore's setup changed in 2026 and the top search results are stale. It now uses `iloader` on the computer plus `LocalDevVPN` from the App Store. The jitterbugpair.exe / .mobiledevicepairing / StosVPN+WireGuard flow that dominates Google is the LEGACY path — following it will waste hours.

Order of operations that minimises wasted App IDs: (1) push a 20-line HealthKit stub, get the unsigned IPA, sideload it, confirm the authorization sheet appears. (2) only then add App Groups + the extension. (3) only then write the real app. Each install cycle is metered against a 10-per-week ceiling that you cannot buy your way out of on a free ID, so treat CI iterations as free and DEVICE installs as scarce.
